decisions.reason: The particle-therapy water phantom is technologically close to the firm's dosimetry and QA capabilities, but its niche market, earlier staged rollout, and lack of later visibility make it the most plausible candidate for withdrawal if commercialization stays weak.

This small-volume ionization chamber remains strongly aligned with the firm's core detector, calibration, and clinical support knowledge, so management would usually retain it unless demand proved persistently too limited.

Because this chamber also builds on existing absorptive capacity in ion chambers and service infrastructure, the firm is more likely to refine and support it than exit, though some rationalization risk remains after limited later visibility.

A standard clinical ionization chamber line sits at the heart of the firm's established business and benefits from broad customer fit, making discontinuation within the coming year relatively unlikely.

An ionization chamber for relative dosimetry is a natural extension of the firm's long-standing measurement expertise, so management would typically keep it and learn from use unless sales were clearly disappointing.
The thimble ionization chamber is a classic, highly related product for this firm, and its calibration, accreditation, and support capabilities make continued marketing more likely than withdrawal.
